title: Seven decades, 33 moments
lede: From a television counter in a tire store to a web shop with the old logo. Filter by thread.

events.title: Wards opens in Richmond
events.text: Sam Wurtzel begins selling televisions from the front half of a tire store on Broad Street.

events.title: Wards goes public
events.text: The share sale pays for a national expansion through licensed departments in discount stores.

events.title: Alan Wurtzel becomes CEO
events.text: After a near-bankruptcy in 1975 he closes weak outlets and builds the superstore format.

events.title: Wards Company becomes Circuit City Stores
events.text: The date of the name change recorded on the company’s SEC filings.

events.title: Richard Sharp succeeds Wurtzel
events.text: Sales are about $1 billion a year, from 69 stores.

events.title: First CarMax opens in Richmond
events.text: A used-car superstore with fixed prices, owned by Circuit City.

events.title: 251 superstores
events.text: Plus 34 mall stores, most of them renamed Circuit City Express that year.

events.title: Best Buy passes Circuit City in revenue
events.text: Best Buy reports $7.2B for its fiscal 1996. The Circuit City stores report $6.75B.

events.title: $100 million more for Divx
events.text: With an earlier $30 million, it gives Circuit City about two-thirds of Digital Video Express.

events.title: circuitcity.com starts selling
events.text: The 10-K dates the launch of the web store to 1999.

events.title: Divx is shut down
events.text: The venture cites a lack of studio support. Buyers of Divx players are offered a $100 rebate.

events.title: Fiscal 2000: the high point for profit
events.text: Circuit City’s continuing operations earn $271 million on $10.5 billion of sales.

events.title: Alan McCollough becomes CEO
events.text: He succeeds Sharp as chief executive.

events.title: Exit from major appliances
events.text: The category was 14% of fiscal 2000 sales. Exit costs are $30 million.

events.title: CarMax separated
events.text: Holders of Circuit City stock receive 0.314 of a CarMax share for each share.

events.title: Commissions end
events.text: The sales force moves to hourly pay only. The Richmond Fed reports 3,900 dismissals in one day.

events.title: InterTAN bought for $259.3 million
events.text: The Canadian chain is later renamed The Source by Circuit City. The store credit card business is sold to Bank One the same month.

events.title: Buyback authorisation reaches $1.2 billion
events.text: The fourth increase since January 2003.

events.title: Seven superstores to close
events.text: Part of a restructuring that also brings a $92 million write-down of the Canadian business.

events.title: 3,400 store employees dismissed
events.text: The “wage management initiative.” IT infrastructure is outsourced to IBM the same day.

events.title: 682 superstores, the most ever
events.text: The fiscal year ends with a net loss of $319.9 million.

events.title: Blockbuster offers at least $6 a share
events.text: It says it first made the offer in a letter on February 17.

events.title: Blockbuster withdraws
events.text: After due diligence, it says a deal is not in its shareholders’ interest.

events.title: Schoonover out
events.text: James Marcum, a director nominated by activist investor Mark Wattles, becomes acting CEO.

events.title: 155 stores to close
events.text: The company says vendors are restricting credit and some want payment before shipment.

events.title: Chapter 11
events.text: Filed in Richmond with a commitment for $1.1 billion of debtor-in-possession financing.

events.title: “Circuit City Stores, Inc. To Liquidate”
events.text: No going-concern deal is reached. The court approves closing 567 stores and distribution centers.

events.title: Going-out-of-business sales end
events.text: The liquidators finish at the last stores.

events.title: Systemax buys the name
events.text: $14.0 million in cash plus a revenue share guaranteed at $3.0 million or more.

events.title: Liquidating trust takes over
events.text: The plan becomes effective and the remaining directors resign.

events.title: Systemax retires the brand
events.text: U.S. consumer operations are consolidated under TigerDirect.

events.title: Name sold again, for $2.0 million
events.text: The buyer is not named in Systemax’s annual report.

events.title: A relaunch is announced at CES
events.text: Chief executive Ronny Shmoel promises a new website on February 15 and, later, kiosks and showrooms.
